questions: Does the edge reversal operation toggle the direction of every edge in the entire graph globally, or only the edges incident to the current vertex?
Is the edge reversal operation allowed at any time, or only when there is no outgoing edge from the current vertex to move along?
After reversing edges, can you immediately reverse again (paying X again) to revert to the original orientations?
If an edge is reversed, does it stay reversed indefinitely until another reversal operation is performed?
Are self-loop edges (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how do they behave under reversal?
Is the goal to minimize total cost, or is there a deterministic sequence implied by the problem statement?
Can you move along an edge and then immediately reverse edges in the same step, or are operations strictly sequential with cost summed?
Is the graph static aside from the reversal operation, or can edges be added/removed by other means?
